comparison: Both support the discovery and functional characterization of TcaP. OpenEval R1 focuses on converging evidence from TEM, plaque assays, and escape mutants (C3-C5, C92), while Peer R1 encompasses broader functional claims including deletion/complementation (C6-C9) and heterologous assembly (C12-C14). Peer reviewers emphasize the comprehensive, high-quality nature of the work.

OpenEval R2 addresses necessity through deletion, complementation, and transduction assays (C6-C9), finding them supported. Peer R1 includes these same claims as part of the broader functional characterization and affirms them without concerns. Both evaluations align in supporting these genetic and functional data.

Both address PLE's unique dependency on TcaP. OpenEval R2 includes comparison to other satellites (C9) and transduction assays (C8) as supported. Peer R8 marks these same claims as UNCERTAIN, noting the observation is interesting but 'it is not clear why this is the case,' indicating incomplete mechanistic understanding despite accepting the observation.

Both address the heterologous assembly system controls. OpenEval R3 evaluates the systematic evidence from the platform (C10-C14, C93) as supported. Peer R2 focuses specifically on the control experiments (C10-C11) and accepts them without question as validation of the system.

OpenEval R3 addresses sufficiency evidence from heterologous assembly (C12-C14, C93). Peer R1 includes these claims within the broader functional characterization, affirming the discovery and functional analysis. Both evaluations support these findings.

Both address scaffold dependencies. OpenEval R3 includes C93 (TcaP's sufficiency and dominance) as supported by heterologous assembly data. Peer R9 includes C93 among inferences about portal and scaffold dependencies, accepting them without question as supporting the proposed model.

Perfect match on escape mutant behavior in heterologous system (C15, C94). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval emphasizes how the data reconcile in vitro vs in vivo phenotypes, while peer reviewers accept the findings as supporting evidence for TcaP-coat interactions without critique.

Both address structural characterization. OpenEval R5 evaluates high-resolution cryo-EM data (C16-C21) as definitively establishing TcaP structure and function. Peer R4 includes these claims plus comparative structural analysis (C30, C53-C56), unanimously praising the structural work as 'compelling' and 'astonishing,' with only minor modeling incompleteness noted.

Perfect match on genomic analysis of natural isolates (C22). Both evaluations support this finding. OpenEval notes it provides strong evidence that escape mutations are not selected in nature. Peer reviewers accept it as supporting the interpretation that TcaP-mediated capsid remodeling is effective against natural ICP1 populations.

Both address conservation of tcaP across PLEs (C23-C24). OpenEval R7 includes C86 (inference that all PLEs use this strategy) and finds the conservation data supports this conclusion. Peer R6 accepts the comparative genomic finding without critique, supporting generalizability of the TcaP mechanism.

Substantial overlap on PLE5's truncated TcaP. OpenEval R7 addresses sequence, morphology, functional assays, and structural rationalization (C23-C24, C86) as supported. Peer R7 includes these plus restoration data (C25-C29, C83-C86, C90), accepting all findings about PLE5's natural variant and restoration as evolutionary evidence for TcaP importance.

Both address PLE5's nonfunctional TcaP. OpenEval R8 evaluates sequence, morphological, functional, and structural evidence (C25-C27, C83-C85) as converging to support the conclusion. Peer R7 includes these claims plus restoration data (C28-C29, C86, C90) and accepts all findings without challenge.

Both address complementation of PLE5's defect (C28). OpenEval R9 finds the transduction assay data supported and consistent with the hypothesis about small capsids promoting transduction. Peer R7 includes this claim among accepted findings about PLE5's natural history.

Both address restoration of full-length tcaP in contemporary isolates (C29, C90). OpenEval R10 finds the sequence analysis supported and the inference about selective advantage reasonable. Peer R7 includes these claims and accepts them as evolutionary evidence for TcaP importance.

Both address selective advantage of TcaP (C90, C102). OpenEval R10 finds the inference reasonable given restoration and conservation data. Peer R13 includes C102 among evolutionary interpretations and accepts the data on PLE5's natural history as evidence for biological importance of capsid remodeling.

Both address structural comparison and convergent evolution (C30, C53-C56). OpenEval R11 finds the structural comparison from cryo-EM data supported. Peer R4 praises the structural work and notes 'the comparison to Sid provides an illustration of probable convergent evolution,' accepting the convergent evolution argument.

Both address the mechanistic model (C31). OpenEval R12 finds the integrated model well-supported by collective data, though some aspects remain to be tested. Peer R1 includes this claim among the comprehensive functional characterization that reviewers affirm without concerns.

Both address packaging calculations and mechanistic inferences (C64-C65, C97). OpenEval R13 finds the calculations straightforward and the inference about non-infectious partial genomes well-established. Peer R12 accepts these calculations and mechanistic inferences without question, noting the model explains how capsid size reduction inhibits ICP1 while promoting PLE packaging.

Both address PLE5 maintenance and evolutionary dynamics (C66-C67, C87-C89). OpenEval R14 finds the genomic surveillance and transduction data supported, though mechanisms remain speculative (C98-C101). Peer R13 accepts the evolutionary and ecological interpretations without challenge, viewing the data as evidence for biological importance of capsid remodeling.

Both address portal dependency (C81-C82). OpenEval R15 marks these as UNCERTAIN, noting the portal dependency has not been directly tested and remains a hypothesis requiring validation. Peer R9 marks them as SUPPORTED, accepting the inferences about portal and scaffold dependencies without question.

Both address evolutionary dynamics and why escape mutations are not found in nature (C95-C96). OpenEval R16 marks these as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative or based on limited data with alternative explanations existing. Peer R11 marks them as SUPPORTED, accepting the explanations as reasonable hypotheses supported by the data.

Both address mechanisms for PLE5 maintenance (C98-C101). OpenEval R17 marks these as UNCERTAIN, noting they are largely speculative hypotheses for future investigation. Peer R13 includes these among evolutionary interpretations and accepts them as SUPPORTED without challenge.

Peer R10 addresses comparative observations about P2/Sid escape mechanisms (C59-C61) that are not explicitly evaluated in OpenEval results. Reviewers accept these as strengthening the convergent evolution argument.

Peer R14 addresses extensive contextual information about phage satellites and comparative systems (C32-C52, C68-C80, C91, C103-C104) that are not explicitly evaluated in OpenEval results. Reviewers accept this contextual framework as strengthening the manuscript and supporting implications for understanding satellite evolution.
